note: Outlook per graded series: h hopeful, m bittersweet, b bleak. msg = core philosophy line when the entry lacks life_message.

101517.msg: A good life is one where you help others and die surrounded by people, without regret, accepting that you are one "cog" among many who carry the work forward.

34632.msg: The series does not promote a single picture of a good life. It shows how neglect, abuse and isolation damage children, and it suggests that ordinary survival, with work and a few human ties, is what is left after the dream of rescue through one perfect love fails.

30003.msg: Ordinary people have one thing in life they must not run from. A good life means remembering what you did as a child, owning up to it, keeping faith with your friends and refusing to follow a hidden leader just because the crowd does.

30001.msg: Every human life has equal worth, and the duty to save it does not depend on who the person is or what they have done. A good life is choosing that, again and again, even toward a monster, while refusing to become one.

87170.msg: A life is worth living even in pain, and people may need to choose (or act) a role to keep going; revenge, cults and saviors built on lies destroy the people inside them.

85611.msg: Life is a series of choices whose results must be carried, not undone; a person who accepts his own sins and chooses to live can help build a world where enemies live together, and a family is worth living for.

74489.msg: A self is made by its losses and its bonds, and wanting to be someone, to be useful and to fix everything, can cause great suffering. Empathy for every kind of being matters most, and peace may come only by letting the self go.

54705.msg: The series does not hold up a single good life. It shows the adolescent wish to escape an empty, conformist world ("the other side of the mountain") as real and understandable, follows it to the edge of death, and then suggests that a livable life comes from facing what one did, accepting it, and making something (writing, a relationship) out of it.

169355.msg: A good life honors the family bond and turns rage over a murdered parent into the protection of others; inherited power must be faced honestly, including the wrongs it did.

105469.msg: A good life is lived for others and with others: love should free the beloved rather than bind them, and a wounded person can turn their pain into protecting people.

98397.msg: The series holds up no ideal good life. It argues that love which possesses another person destroys both, that a child must somehow become a separate self to live at all, and that the "tracks" of harm passed from parent to child can at least be seen, understood and allowed to stop, even when they cannot be undone.

30149.msg: Persistence matters even when the world is vast, hostile and indifferent. Humanity, however altered, is worth restoring, and hope is handed on in the form of a new life rather than won by a final victory.

86082.msg: A good life is a fed, shared and honest one. Eat what you take, waste nothing, accept your place in the food chain and your own mortality, and let desire and appetite keep you alive without letting them rule you.

30336.msg: A good teacher, and a good adult, meets each young person as a person: he takes their pain seriously, keeps his word, takes the blows for them and refuses to let a system decide who they are. Rules, rank and test scores matter less than loyalty and guts.

33731.msg: A good life does not need a big dream to come true. It is made of honest work, friends, music and the people you love, held lightly because they do not last; grief is survived by carrying the dead person's song forward rather than by escaping.
